attribution: Credited to the work the manuscript cites, not to OpenAI or the manuscript's authors. The manuscript says: “We use Dinur’s perfect-completeness formulation [7, Definition 8.1 and Theorem 8.1, February 13, 2007 author manuscript].” Its bibliography: “[7] Irit Dinur. The PCP theorem by gap amplification. Journal of the ACM, 54(3), June 2007. Article 12, 44 pages. Definition 8.1 and Theorem 8.1 are cited in the author manuscript dated February 13, 2007, p. 27: https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~dinuri/mypapers/ combpcp.pdf.” Quoted from openai/math (Apache-2.0); AMVO has not consulted or checked the cited work.
scope: Theorem 2.1 (Perfect-completeness PCP gap) of the manuscript “Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games” (preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 105 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2691ba6bd2ac7159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a constant γ0 > 0 and a deterministic polynomial-time map taking any Boolean 3-CNF formula φ to a nonempty 3-CNF formula Ψ such that every clause of Ψ uses three distinct variables. If φ is satisfiable, then Ψ is satisfiable. If φ is unsatisfiable, every assignment violates at least a γ0 fraction of the clauses of Ψ. Clause occurrences are explicitly listed, and the binary encoding length of Ψ is polynomial in that of φ.
